note: PRIVATE ground truth. Read only by the validator and the grader; never shown to benchmarked agents. All tasks are Type B (injected incidents): see README for why no Type A tasks were kept.

expected.root_cause: Order 72902's ship-to address (shiptoaddressid) points to address 11431 (8, rue des Vendangeurs, Paris), which belongs to a different customer (Laura Cai, person 2411 / customer 21113), not to the ordering customer. The ship-to address on the order was set to the wrong address record.
required_facts: Order 72902 belongs to customer 11878 (Christine Nara, person 19889).
The order's shiptoaddressid is 11431, an address in Paris, France.
Address 11431 is linked to another person/customer (Laura Cai, 2411 / customer 21113), not to Christine Nara.
The customer's own (only) address is 28990 in Ballard, Washington; it is still the bill-to address of 72902 and was the ship-to of her earlier order 72001.
not_root_cause: The customer moved or has a French address on file

expected.root_cause: Every unit received on PO 2467 was rejected: on both detail lines rejectedqty equals receivedqty, so nothing was accepted into stock (and no inventory receipt transactions exist for the PO).
required_facts: PO 2467 has status 4 (complete).
Both lines show receivedqty equal to rejectedqty (all received units rejected), 1,100 units in total.
There are no receipt ('P') transactions in production.transactionhistory for PO 2467.
not_root_cause: The goods were never shipped or received

expected.root_cause: Britta Simon has two open department history rows: her Production assignment (since 2009-01-29) was never end-dated when a Quality Assurance assignment starting 2025-03-03 was added.
required_facts: Employee 30 has two employeedepartmenthistory rows with enddate NULL.
One is Production (department 7) starting 2009-01-29; the other is Quality Assurance (department 13) starting 2025-03-03.
The old Production row should have been closed (end-dated) when the new assignment began.
not_root_cause: Two separate employee records for the same person

expected.root_cause: Yes. The Sport-100 Helmet, Blue line (salesorderdetailid 119272) was charged a unit price of 349.90 instead of the 34.99 list price in effect on the order date - a decimal-shift (10x) pricing error. The order totals include the overcharge (314.91 on the subtotal).
required_facts: Line 119272 (product 711, Sport-100 Helmet, Blue, qty 1) has unitprice 349.90.
The list price effective on the order date (productlistpricehistory / product.listprice) is 34.99.
The overcharge is 314.91 before tax and freight; the order subtotal/total include it.
not_root_cause: The customer ordered a different quantity

expected.root_cause: The HL Mountain Pedal (product 937) has exactly one approved supplier in productvendor, Inline Accessories (vendor 1638), and that vendor is now inactive (activeflag = false).
required_facts: Product 937's only productvendor row is for vendor 1638, Inline Accessories.
Vendor 1638 has activeflag = false.
The product itself is not discontinued (no sell end / discontinued date).

expected.root_cause: The customer record itself was reassigned: sales.customer 12961 now has territoryid 5 (Southeast), changed on 2025-05-15, although the customer's only address is still in Beaverton, Oregon (Northwest). Orders take the customer's territory, so the June order 74780 was booked to Southeast while the April order 70034 was Northwest.
required_facts: Customer 12961 has territoryid 5 (Southeast) with a modified date of 2025-05-15.
The customer's address (Beaverton, Oregon) is in a state/province that belongs to the Northwest territory (1).
Order 70034 (April 2025) has territory 1; order 74780 (June 2025) has territory 5; both ship to the same address.
not_root_cause: A salesperson assignment (online orders have no salesperson)

expected.root_cause: Order 74509 was charged to credit card 18027, which belongs to another person (Arturo Sun, person 10006 / customer 11498) according to sales.personcreditcard. The customer's own card is 11266, which was used on all four of their other orders.
required_facts: Order 74509 (2025-06-10, customer 14282) has creditcardid 18027.

expected.root_cause: The price history for product 877 has two open-ended rows: the new 8.95 row starting 2025-06-01 was added, but the previous 7.95 row (start 2024-05-29) was never end-dated, so the old price remains effective and was used for June orders.

product.listprice is 8.95.

expected.root_cause: Transaction 196618 (type S) records 300 units of Front Brakes for sales order 71775, but that order's line for product 948 is for only 3 units. The inventory transaction quantity was entered 100x too high; the sales order itself is correct.
required_facts: Transaction 196618 is a sales ('S') transaction for product 948 on 2025-04-30 with quantity 300.
Its referenceorderid 71775 is a sales order whose Front Brakes line has orderqty 3.
The discrepancy is in the transaction record (quantity), not the order.

productvendor has no row for product 941 and vendor 1636; the only supplier is vendor 1628 (Bicycle Specialists).
Integrated Sport Products supplies clothing/accessories, not pedals.

expected.root_cause: Patrick Cook's (employee 83) position in the organization hierarchy was changed: his organizationnode is /1/1/8/, which places him directly under /1/1/, the Engineering Manager (Roberto Tamburello, employee 3). His job title (Production Technician - WC40) and department history (Production) are unchanged, so he should sit under a WC40 production supervisor (his original supervisor was Reuben D'sa, employee 78, /3/1/7/; the data no longer records which one, so naming any WC40 Production Supervisor as the expected manager is acceptable). The hierarchy node was mis-set (employee record modified 2025-05-12) without any actual transfer.
required_facts: Employee 83 has organizationnode /1/1/8/, whose parent /1/1/ is the Engineering Manager (Roberto Tamburello, employee 3).
He is still a 'Production Technician - WC40' in the Production department (no department change).

expected.root_cause: The bill of materials for Mountain-200 Black, 38 (product 782) was changed on 2025-04-01: the size-38 frame (747, HL Mountain Frame - Black, 38) was end-dated 2025-03-31 and replaced by the size-46 frame (746, HL Mountain Frame - Black, 46). Assemblies are built with a frame of the wrong size, so every work order since April is scrapped; the 'Drill pattern incorrect' scrap reason is a symptom of the mismatched frame, not of the drilling equipment.
required_facts: BOM row for assembly 782 / component 747 ends 2025-03-31; a new row for component 746 (size 46) starts 2025-04-01.
All 47 work orders for 782 starting 2025-04-01 or later are fully scrapped with scrap reason 'Drill pattern incorrect'; earlier work orders had essentially no scrap.
The other Mountain-200 sizes/colors have no comparable scrap spike, and their BOMs keep matching frames.
not_root_cause: Operator error at a work center

expected.root_cause: Order 53451 contains a duplicated line: Touring-2000 Blue, 60 (product 953) appears twice (detail 46745 and a second line 121318) for 2 units at 728.91 each, so the order subtotal includes an extra 1,457.82. The duplicate was added later (modified 2024-08-13) and has no matching shipment transaction - only one shipment of 2 units exists. The Touring-3000 promotion discount on the other line is legitimate and not the cause.
required_facts: Order 53451 has two identical lines for product 953 (2 units at 728.91).
The extra line adds 1,457.82 to the subtotal (more with tax and freight).
Only one sales transaction (2 units of product 953) exists for order 53451; the second line was never shipped.
The 15% Touring-3000 promotion on product 965 is a valid discount, not the problem.
not_root_cause: The promotional discount was applied incorrectly

expected.root_cause: Order 73806 references currency rate 12377, which is the USD->JPY rate (119.84) for 2025-05-25, instead of the USD->GBP rate 12376 (0.6282) used by the other UK orders that day. The United Kingdom's currency is GBP (countryregioncurrency), so the order's local-currency conversion uses the wrong currency.
required_facts: Order 73806 (territory United Kingdom) has currencyrateid 12377.
Rate 12377 converts USD to JPY (averagerate 119.84), not GBP.
Other UK orders on 2025-05-25 use rate 12376 (USD->GBP, 0.6282); GB's currency is GBP.
not_root_cause: The customer is not in the UK

product 707's standard cost (130.863) exceeds its list price (34.99).

PO 4013 was created later (modified 2025-06-24) and is out of sequence with surrounding PO ids.
